Natural gums, resins, gum-resins and oleoresins fall in heading 1301 (lac; natural gums, resins, gum-resins and oleoresins such as balsams). Subheading 1301.90 covers "Other", and 1301.90.90 is "Other" within it. Frankincense (olibanum) is a gum-resin, so it belongs here.

The statistical suffix under 1301.90.90 is 1301.90.9086 for other natural gums, resins, gum-resins, and oleoresins. I recall this as 1301.90.90 with the suffix 90 for "Other", but I am not certain of the exact suffix. Heading 1301 breaks down as follows:
- 1301.20.00 Gum Arabic
- 1301.90.10 Natural gums (other)
- 1301.90.20 Tragacanth?
- 1301.90.40 Cannabis?
- 1301.90.90 Other

I believe the lines are 1301.90.10 (Dragon's blood?), 1301.90.20 (Karaya?), 1301.90.90 (Other), with the statistical suffix 1301.90.9050 or 1301.90.9090. I'll go with 1301.90.9090.

Incense-use classification under 3307 (preparations for perfuming or deodorizing rooms) would apply only to prepared incense. Since this is an unprocessed resin, 1301 is appropriate.
